A R T I C L E I N F O

Numerical simulation
Raman spectra
A B S T R A C T
Achieving cobalt superconformal (bottom-up) growth is significantly important. Electrochemical methods,
including cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectra and EQCM-derived Coulomb-voltage curves,
were used to confirm the suppressing influence of new suppressor Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride (NBT). In situ
Raman spectroscopy was used confirm that NBT can effectively adsorb on cobalt surface. Besides, EQCM-derived
Coulomb-voltage illustrates that it is more beneficial for cobalt electrodeposition at high pH. The NBT effect on
hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) was studied by LSV and chronoamperometry. Finite element simulation is
used to investigate the accelerating effect of NBT on HER and convection. Suppressing-accelerating effect is
proposed to illustrate effect of NBT. NBT can not only suppress the cobalt deposition but also can accelerate local
convection by intensifying HER, which can in turn strengthen NBT adsorption. SEM analysis demonstrates that
convection and NBT can refine grain. High-quality cobalt is achieved with low SDT values ranging from 24 μm to
45 μm and high FP values (75.4 % for 150 μm, 88.9 % for 100 μm and 87.2 % for 50 μm)

tering at the boundary [7,8], which increases the IC delay and has a bad
influence on electronic property [9,10]. As a result, developing new-
generation interconnect metal is industrially important [11]. Cobalt,
due to its low MFEP and compatibility with copper damascene tech-
nology, has been used as the interconnect metal at advanced node
Due to uneven distribution of electric field caused by edge effect and

achieve superconformal growth based electrochemical methods [16],

tance (S-NDR) model to predict bottom-up filling [17]. In contrast,

mechanism to illustrate the influence of malachite green on bottom-up

used to study the adsorption of additives. Besides, HER occurs inevitably
during cobalt electrodeposition and has a significant influence on local
mass transfer. Nevertheless, there is lack of research on the effect of HER
during electrodeposition and the influence of additive on HER [24,25].
Nowadays, finite element method (FEM) is widely used to simulate the
practical process to provide more detailed information for researchers
[26], like diffusion [27], electric field distribution [28,29], gas releasing
process [30], TSV filling simulation [31,32] and so on. Li et al combined
experimental and simulated results to propose Gas Microfluidic Pump-
ing (GMP) model to illustrate the effect of gas releasing during HER on
the mass transfer [33]. As a result, applying FEM is a good way to help
researcher to understand the influence of HER on mass transfer.
In this work, we use cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical
impedance spectra (EIS) and EQCM-derived Coulomb-voltage to inves-
tigate Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride (NBT) suppressing effect of during
electrodeposition. The adsorption phenomena of NBT on were
confirmed by in situ Raman spectra was used to verify the possible
adsorption of NBT on cathode during electrodeposition. The influence of
pH on current density was studied by measuring EQCM-derived
Coulomb-voltage curves, while the acceleration of NBT on HER was
analyzed and the influence of gas flow produced by HER with different
NBT concentration on flow rate (convection) of electrolytes was ac-
quired by Finite element simulation. Scanning electron micrograph
(SEM) was used to observe the convection and NBT on cobalt layer
morphology. Finally, superconformal filling in microvias is achieved.
2. Experiments
2.1. Materials and chemicals
In this work, analytical grade (AR) additive Nitrotetrazolium Blue
chloride (NBT) with CAS no. of 298–83-9 is bought from Shanghai
Aladdin Co., Ltd., China, while other AR chemicals, including
\mathrm { C o S O _ { 4 } { \cdot } 7 H _ { 2 } O , H _ { 3 } B O _ { 3 } }
and NaCl, is purchased from Sinopharm Chemical
Reagent Co. Ltd., China. The deionized water is used to prepare all kinds
of electroplating solutions.
2.2. Electrochemical measurement
Electrochemical measurement was controlled by Gamry Framework
and was measured in a traditional three-electrode system. The rotating
disk electrode (radius of 0.25 cm), saturated mercury sulfate electrode
(SSE) and a platinum with the area of 2 cm × 1 cm were used as working,
reference and counter electrode, respectively. Inert
\mathrm { N } _ { 2 }
was pumped into
bath solution to remove oxygen dissolved to exclude the possible oxi-
dization influence before electrochemical tests. The scan rate for cyclic
voltammetry (CV) is 5 mV/s and the rotating speed was 1000 rpm, while
electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) was carried out at 1.25 V v.s.
SSE, 500 rpm. The scan rate for linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV) was
5 mV/s. Besides, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM)
was used to study NBT effect on cobalt deposition with 5 MHz gold
quartz crystal. Before carrying EQCM tests, the gold quartz crystal was
pre plated with cobalt layer at

for 60 s. Current transients was
carried out by chronoamperometry at different cathodic potentials.
2.3. Finite element simulation
Finite element (FE) simulation was carried out by COMSOL Multi-
physics. Two-dimensional symmetric model was established to simulate
the rotating disk electrode (RDE). The radius of simulated RDE is set as
0.25 cm according to experiments. Electrochemistry module and CFD
module were coupled together to simulate the influence of HER with
different NBT concentration on the mass transfer of NBT. Tertiary cur-
rent distribution and bubble flow and laminar flow were used, respec
tively. The parameters (exchange current density, charge transfer
efficient) were calculated from LSV curves obtained with different NBT
concentration and the detailed parameters were shown in Table S1.

The NBT adsorption behavior on cobalt surface was studied by in situ
Raman spectra at RENISHAW with excitation wavelength of
nm.
Gamry Framework station was used to control the cathodic potentials.
The surface morphology under the influence of NBT and convection was
measured on scanning electron microscope (Helios Nanolab 600i).

asserted in Fig. 7. Fig. 7 (a) shows that the cobalt layer consists of
rectangular strip grain without NBT. The cobalt surface is loose and the
grain size is relatively large with mean grain size about 321 nm.

302 nm), the cobalt layer is not so compact due to the rectangular strip

result, the convection and NBT can effectively improve the cobalt
morphology.

3.5. Electroplating
Electroplating is carried out to verify this new suppressor, namely
NBT. Fig. 8 shows the shape evolution of microvias with different di
ameters during cobalt electroplating. The surface deposit thickness
(SDT) and filling percentage (FP) are used to judge the filling perfor
The shape evolution of cobalt layer in microvias of 150 μm is shown
in Fig. 8 (a). a2 in Fig. 2 (a) shows that the deposition of cobalt at the
opening and plane is suppressed obviously after being electrodeposited
for 4 h. The SDT and FP is 45.0 μm and 75.4 % when cobalt layer is
electrodeposited for 10 h. The relatively high FP value and low SDT
indicate that cobalt layer is of high quality.
Likewise, it can be seen from b2 and c2 that the cobalt grows faster at
the bottom than on the sidewalls and opening of the microvias, which is
attributed to the intensified mass transfer of NBT at the opening and
sidewalls, while the consuming rate of NBT at the bottom is higher than
the supplementary rate at the bottom. Hence, cobalt grows from bottom
to up. After being electrodeposited for 8 h for 100 μm (b3) and 6 h for 50
μm (c3), cobalt layer reaches to the opening and the FP values are high
(88.9 % and 87.2 %, respectively) with SDT for 100 μm and 50 μm being
30.7 μm and 24.9 μm.
Suppressing-accelerating effect was proposed to clearly illustrate the
filling mechanism of NBT. On one hand, it is NBT who plays a major
effect in superfilling process because growth rate difference at the plane
and in the bottom can be caused due to effective NBT concentration
gradient is formed as a result of geometry limitation and mass transfer
limitation (suppressing effect). On the other hand, the accelerating ef
fect of NBT on HER will play a supporting role during electroplating.
Because the mass transfer at the plane is influenced little compared with
that in the microvias due to geometry limitation. The NBT concentration
at the plane is relatively higher, which strengthen the HER and gas
releasing process in turn further intensify the NBT diffusion and
adsorption to suppress the cobalt deposition at the plane. In contrast, the
mass transfer is limited in microvias, leading to the NBT concentration is
relatively low, which weaken the hydrogen bubble releasing and in turn
lower the supplying of NBT from bulk to feature. The cobalt begins to
grow from the bottom to the top. The accelerating effect has a positive
influence on cobalt interconnect layer quality. In summary, the rela-
tively low SDT and high FP values obtained in microvias with different
diameters indicate that high-quality cobalt interconnect layer can be
achieved under the influence of NBT.
4. Conclusion
In this work, electrochemical analysis methods, including cyclic
voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectra and EQCM were used
to study the suppressing effect of NBT on cobalt electrodeposition. Be-
sides, in situ Raman spectra was used to analyze the suppressing mech-
anism and NBT can absorb on cobalt surface to suppress the cobalt
electrodeposition. EQCM-derived coulomb-voltage curves indicates that
high pH is beneficial for the cobalt electrodeposition. Finite element
method was accepted to simulate the influence of NBT concentration on
convection. Besides, NBT can benefit the HER, which can effectively
intensify the local mass transfer during electrodeposition. The intensi-
fied local mass transfer can further supply suppressor NBT to cathode
surface so as keep the deposition in plane suppressed. Suppressing-
accelerating effect is proposed to illustrate the effect of NBT. On one
hand, NBT can adsorb on cathode surface to suppress cobalt deposition.
On the other hand, NBT can boost the HER and the intensified gas
releasing process in turn accelerate the mass transfer of NBT to
strengthen the suppressing effect of NBT on cobalt electrodeposition.

4. Conclusion
In this work, electrochemical analysis methods, including cyclic
voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectra and EQCM were used
to study the suppressing effect of NBT on cobalt electrodeposition. Be-
sides, in situ Raman spectra was used to analyze the suppressing mech-
anism and NBT can absorb on cobalt surface to suppress the cobalt
electrodeposition. EQCM-derived coulomb-voltage curves indicates that
high pH is beneficial for the cobalt electrodeposition. Finite element
method was accepted to simulate the influence of NBT concentration on
convection. Besides, NBT can benefit the HER, which can effectively
intensify the local mass transfer during electrodeposition. The intensi-
fied local mass transfer can further supply suppressor NBT to cathode
surface so as keep the deposition in plane suppressed. Suppressing-
accelerating effect is proposed to illustrate the effect of NBT. On one
hand, NBT can adsorb on cathode surface to suppress cobalt deposition.
On the other hand, NBT can boost the HER and the intensified gas
releasing process in turn accelerate the mass transfer of NBT to
strengthen the suppressing effect of NBT on cobalt electrodeposition.
The effect of convection and NBT on cobalt layer is investigated by SEM
as well as convection and NBT is conducive to refine the grain size.
Superconformal growth was obtained within different microvias with
relatively good quality. The SDT values for for 150 μm, 100 μm and 50
μm are low (45.0 μm, 30.7 μm and 24.9 μm, respectively), while the FP
values are 75.4 % for 150 μm, 88.9 % for 100 μm and 87.2 % for 50 μm.
